data.body:
TDD contract card and parity census for 742d:

- authoritative_contract: ticket ACs plus current workflow red-on-persistent-failure behavior and the landed private CLI in src/rebar/_store/push.py.
- trigger_preconditions: reconciler exact run block starts with a dirty real tracker under project sync.push=off; canary exact run block starts clean but one commit ahead; strict-failure cases use a real bare origin with a rejecting pre-receive hook.
- production_path: parse each named GitHub Actions step, substitute only the run-id expression, and execute the exact shell with the worktree venv against real temporary git repositories.
- test_tier: executable workflow subprocess + real git refs; a source-only assertion is one tier too low because it cannot prove argparse, env, commit identity, delivery, exit code, or pending-commit behavior.
- observable_postcondition: reconciler exits 0, pushes the dirty event, and the remote commit has the exact subject and supplied author despite sync.push=off; rejection exits nonzero and keeps the local commit. Canary pushes an ahead commit; policy rejection exits nonzero and keeps it pending.
- collateral_invariants: unrelated files and remote history remain intact; no empty commit; working tree clean after successful reconciler commit; rejected local commit remains reachable.
- negative_control: project sync.push=off without the workflow's REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always would not deliver; the exact block must override it.
- recovery/contention: no new retry implementation is introduced; both calls ride the already-locked core seam, so existing in-process push suites own rejection→fetch→merge→re-push contention. No new contention harness is warranted.
- ci_gate: exact nodes collected/executed under make test; focused run first, then make lint/typecheck/test.

Surface parity: CLI/private process boundary = in scope through both exact workflow blocks; automated callers = in scope, one executable test per workflow; library facade = out of scope/no contract change, existing best-effort tests retained; MCP/API = out of scope/no call-path change; dual-direction/inbound Jira application = out of scope because this cutover changes only outbound tickets delivery.
